blocks.title: The cell cycle
blocks.md: The **cell cycle** is the sequence of events from one cell division to the next. **Interphase** has **G1** (cell growth, protein synthesis), **S** (DNA replication) and **G2** (preparation, organelles doubled). **Mitosis** follows, then **cytokinesis**. Checkpoints control progress; cells that stop dividing enter G0.

blocks.title: Chromosome or chromatid?
blocks.md: After replication each chromosome consists of **two sister chromatids** joined at the centromere. In anaphase the chromatids separate and each is then called a chromosome. The chromosome number does not double at the start of mitosis; it is the amount of DNA that doubled in S phase. Mitosis gives cells with the **same** number of chromosomes as the parent (2n → 2n).

items.text: The cell cycle: interphase then mitosis

blocks.caption: The cell cycle: interphase followed by the four stages of mitosis.
blocks.alt: Five boxes in a row: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase, joined by arrows.

blocks.title: Stages of mitosis
blocks.md:
- **Prophase**: chromosomes condense; nuclear envelope breaks; spindle forms.
- **Metaphase**: chromosomes line up at the equator, attached by centromeres.
- **Anaphase**: centromeres divide; chromatids pulled to poles.
- **Telophase**: nuclear envelopes reform; chromosomes uncoil.
- **Cytokinesis**: cytoplasm divides (cleavage furrow in animals, cell plate in plants).

blocks.title: Roles and cancer
blocks.md: Mitosis gives growth, tissue repair and asexual reproduction (e.g. cassava stem cuttings). **Cancer** is uncontrolled division caused by mutation in genes controlling the cell cycle. The **mitotic index** (cells in mitosis ÷ total cells) is higher in tumours and in growing root tips.

blocks.title: Worked example — mitotic index
blocks.statement: In a root-tip squash, 150 cells are counted and 18 are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index.
steps: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells.

blocks.title: Worked example — DNA content
blocks.statement: A human diploid cell has 46 chromosomes. How many chromatids are present at metaphase, and how many chromosomes in each daughter cell?
steps: At metaphase each of the 46 chromosomes has two chromatids: 46 × 2 = 92.

blocks.title: Meiosis
blocks.md: **Meiosis** is the cell division that produces four **haploid** (n) gametes or spores from a **diploid** (2n) cell. DNA is replicated once, but the nucleus divides twice. In **meiosis I** homologous chromosomes pair (forming **bivalents**) and separate; in **meiosis II** sister chromatids separate, as in mitosis.

blocks.title: Homologues versus chromatids
blocks.md: In meiosis I it is **homologous chromosomes** that separate (one maternal, one paternal), not chromatids. The cells at the end of meiosis I are already haploid, but each chromosome still has two chromatids. Chromatids separate in meiosis II. Do not confuse **crossing over** (exchange between non-sister chromatids in prophase I) with independent assortment (random orientation in metaphase I).

items.text: Meiosis I: homologues separate (2 cells, n)

blocks.caption: Meiosis in outline: from one diploid cell to four haploid cells.
blocks.alt: Four boxes in a vertical chain from a diploid cell through meiosis I and II to four haploid cells.

blocks.title: Sources of variation
blocks.md:
- **Crossing over** at chiasmata: new combinations of alleles on each chromosome.
- **Independent assortment**: for n pairs of chromosomes there are 2ⁿ possible combinations (for humans 2²³ = 8 388 608) before crossing over is counted.
- **Random fertilisation**: any sperm can fuse with any egg.
- Mutation provides new alleles.

blocks.title: Mitosis versus meiosis
blocks.md: Mitosis: one division, two cells, diploid, identical, growth and repair. Meiosis: two divisions, four cells, haploid, genetically different, makes gametes; homologues pair and cross over. **Non-disjunction** (failure of chromosomes to separate) gives gametes with an extra or missing chromosome, e.g. trisomy 21.

blocks.title: Worked example — combinations
blocks.statement: An organism has 4 pairs of chromosomes (2n = 8). How many different combinations of chromosomes can its gametes have by independent assortment alone?
steps: Each pair can orient in 2 ways.

blocks.title: Worked example — chromosome numbers
blocks.statement: A cell of a maize plant has 20 chromosomes (2n = 20). Give the number of chromosomes in a cell after meiosis I, after meiosis II, and in the zygote.
steps: Meiosis I halves the number: 20 → 10 per cell.
Meiosis II separates chromatids, so each cell still has 10 chromosomes (now single).
Two gametes with 10 chromosomes fuse: zygote 10 + 10 = 20.
